summary: Improve credit EWS design, trigger calibration, and portfolio reporting through five days of applied banking risk exercises. View the course outline.
lede: Banking early warning systems combine borrower, facility, and portfolio indicators to flag emerging credit deterioration. For credit risk officers, portfolio monitoring leads, and model validators, the training focuses on designing and challenging a consistent process for reviewing signals and escalating cases. Participants practise selecting indicators, calibrating explainable triggers, analyzing portfolio trends, and documenting data lineage and validation evidence.
audienceIntro: This course suits experienced banking professionals who design, operate, validate, or oversee credit early warning processes. It is especially relevant when your responsibilities include portfolio surveillance, borrower escalation, model governance, or risk reporting.
modules: Banking Early Warning Systems Signal Design
prerequisites: Participants should have practical experience in banking credit risk, portfolio monitoring, credit analysis, model validation, or risk reporting. Familiarity with credit ratings, borrower financial information, and spreadsheet analysis is expected. No programming is required.
